notes: Griffith no. 94: the Meroitic inscription of king Kharamadoye (Griffith's Kharamazeye), 34 lines of very late cursive cut on the second column of the facade of the hall of columns of the great temple, beginning on one drum and ending on the next, with a Greek inscription above and below; height 72 cm. L., D., VI, Bl. 6, no. 21; Pls. XIII-XVI. Griffith: practically complete, ll. 22-23 injured at the joint, right-hand ends of ll. 29-34 chiselled, signs 'not of very distinct forms', lines crowded. He prints ll. 1-3 and the seven parallel phrases of ll. 3-7 phrase by phrase (type lines 1-13), then the running text. His readings bearing on the text: 'sic' over the two-stroke y of qoreyi (l. 4); in l. 8 the stone has e-o-se (sic) where the type prints the corrected yismeniye; in l. 15 the o of ptpoto is 'sic', probably for ':' before t; (:) in l. 28 is his supplied divider; the divider before smle (l. 26) is queried; {sign} after wes (l. 26) is a 'peculiar sign', a numeral or an ill-formed s; l. 21 'much confused'; in l. 31 every sign of a(31)rw and the final ':' are uncertain; l. 33 is almost illegible through chiselling, with 'sic?' over the n of plN. Names and words he identifies: Kharamazeye, qore, Arite(n), Amanitake, Amanapate (mnpte), Amanete (mnote), Makezeke (mkedoke), kharpkhe (xrpxe), Yismeniye, Aqateye, Pakhoras/Faras (pXrs), Shimale/Ibrim (Simlok), Pilqeyte/Philae, Selele, Azere (adere-ke), Azenil (adonili-ke-te), qesw, hrw (Xrw), yireqw, kdileb 'women', Arekhetaye (aroXetye), Patashize (ptSide), Patamakize (ptmkide), Kharêshaye and Yisakhteteye with qo, Wezi (wedi), 'eight kings' (qore 4 4). A word split by Griffith's type-line break or by a superscript line number is joined only where his notes or renderings show one word (aqtoye, ptpotekye, pilqoyte, nsdokes, kedebx, adereke, x(19)rpxe, qe(22)sw, bqob(25)te, bqo(26)bx, wo(34)kle, te(10)pke, t(14)lte, de(24)te); other spaces are as printed.
